LLM auditresponse for languagetool.sh:
<security_assessment>
<decision>SAFE</decision>
<details>
This is a standard wrapper script for the LanguageTool application. It parses command-line arguments, builds a Java classpath from installed JAR files, and launches the appropriate Java main class (CLI, GUI, HTTP server, or HTTPS server) based on user input. The script uses `exec` to replace itself with the Java process, which is normal packaging practice. Arguments like `--http`, `-h`, and `--help` are stripped from the array before passing to Java, which is standard wrapper behavior. No network requests, unauthorized downloads, data exfiltration, or system modifications outside the application scope were detected. The HTML entities (`"`, `'`) appearing in the file content are likely a transmission/display artifact rather than malicious obfuscation, as literal `"` strings would break the script entirely.
</details>
